subject: Pilot runway decision: 21-day buffer or burst-bucket buydown
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anya Lopez <anya@fintraxhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway decision: 21-day buffer or burst-bucket buydown

Hi Anya —

Quick follow from our call this morning. Your squad is through the first two milestones and wants to keep evaluation momentum, but Marcus mentioned procurement is pushing to avoid another time-only addendum. Two concrete options we discussed that finance could evaluate: 

1) 21-day runway buffer (time extension) — same pilot terms, no change to billing cadence. We’d offer a one-time 20% credit on additional days to keep unit economics reasonable.

2) Burst‑bucket buydown (credit SKU) — convert remaining runway into a fixed burst bucket of 100k tokens usable within the next 45 days; discounted unit rate and includes one engineering support block (6 hours). This can be invoiced as a SKU and avoids amending the PO duration.

I attached a rough quote for both options and a one‑page mutual action plan so procurement can see milestones tied to the budget line. Can you confirm which path procurement prefers (time extension vs SKU)? If they want a hybrid we can prototype that too — e.g., 14 days + a smaller burst bucket.

Next steps: if you prefer option 2 I can loop in Kimberly for pricing approval and David to scope the eng hours.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: Fintrax_Pilot_OptionA_quote.pdf, Fintrax_MutualActionPlan.xlsx
From: Anya Lopez <anya@fintraxhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Shaw <marcus.shaw@fintraxhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot runway decision: 21-day buffer or burst-bucket buydown

Thanks, Karthik — appreciate the clear options. Quick notes from procurement and product: 

- Procurement hates open-ended time addenda this quarter; they'd prefer an SKU/invoice line they can route through S4.
- Product likes the burst-bucket idea but wants the bucket to include a small token reservation for model‑level testing (we spike token consumption during eval).
- Would procurement accept a hybrid: convert 50% of the remaining days into a burst bucket and add a 10‑day buffer? They asked for an explicit cost delta to present to legal.

Marcus and I can take a quick numbers sheet — can Kimberly flag what the smallest SKU break you can offer is, and whether the eng hours are refundable if unused?

Best,
Anya Lopez
Director, Product Strategy — Fintrax Health
anya@fintraxhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anya Lopez <anya@fintraxhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway decision: 21-day buffer or burst-bucket buydown

On Tue, Sep 14, 2027 at 12:07 PM Anya Lopez <anya@fintraxhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Karthik — appreciate the clear options. Quick notes from procurement and product: ...

Anya — thanks. Looping in Kimberly and David to get firm numbers. Answers up front:

- Smallest burst SKU we can issue is a 50k-token bucket (we can price a 50k / 100k / 200k tier).
- Eng hours: standard practice is to invoice the block up front; we can offer a 50% refund of unused hours if the team decides after 30 days it's not needed (documented in the mutual action plan).
- Hybrid: we can do 10 days + 50k token bucket with a blended discount (I sketched two pricing lines in the attached quote).

Kimberly — can you confirm the blended discount range I suggested (15% on the burst bucket + convert days at 20% credit) is approved for Fintrax? David — is 6 hours of eng time reasonable to include for the testing reservation?

If procurement signs off on hybrid, I’ll prepare a short addendum that invoices the SKU and appends a 10‑day extension clause.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway decision: 21-day buffer or burst-bucket buydown

Karthik — approving the hybrid structure for this cohort. Conditions:

- Offer: 10-day extension + 50k token burst bucket.
- Pricing: 10‑day extension priced at the same per-day rate as the pilot, with a 20% addendum credit applied to those extra days. The 50k token bucket at a 15% discount to the listed trial SKU.
- Engineering block: 6 hours included; invoice upfront and offer a 50% refund on unused hours after 30 days.
- Legal: no change to SLA; we’ll use an addendum that invoices SKU and attaches the mutual action plan.

Karthik, please translate into a final quote line and confirm the invoicing flow — do we need a PO number on the invoice or will they accept an approved SKU invoice?

Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Shaw <marcus.shaw@fintraxhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Anya Lopez <anya@fintraxhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot runway decision: 21-day buffer or burst-bucket buydown

Thanks, team — this is exactly what procurement needed. Quick clarifying points before we close: 

- PO: procurement will issue a PO for the SKU line (they want the invoice to reference PO# FT-2027-0897).
- Refunds: finance wants the refund term in writing; the 50% refund on unused eng hours is acceptable if documented in the addendum.
- Timing: we’ll approve the hybrid if we receive the invoice and the signed addendum by EOD Monday (20 Sep). Can you confirm you’ll hold pricing for 5 business days?

If Karthik can send a final one-page addendum + invoice referencing PO# FT-2027-0897, we’ll route it to legal and sign.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Marcus Shaw
VP, Procurement — Fintrax Health
marcus.shaw@fintraxhealth.com
